image_description: A vintage typewriter with a cream-colored body and distinctive round, green keys. The image focuses on the keyboard area, showing multiple rows of circular keys with white lettering. At the bottom center is a long, rectangular key (the space bar) that matches the color and style of the other keys but is elongated horizontally.

It is centrally positioned between two other modifier keys (likely shift or margin release keys) on either side. The checkpoint description implies a layout more common to modern computer keyboards, whereas this is a vintage typewriter layout.

Here, it appears to be roughly 3-4 times the diameter of a single round key. The 'ten times' metric is specific to QWERTY computer layouts and fails for this typewriter context.

While recognizable as letters (Q, W, E, R, T, Y...), the edges of the characters bleed slightly into the green background, and some characters lack sharp definition, typical of AI generation struggling with small, high-contrast text details.
